entries.short_title: Knop ALAN pollination networks and focal fruit set
entries.screening_reason: Directly manipulated overnight LEDs, true fruit experiment 5 lit vs 5 dark meadows matched in 5 pairs; 2x2 light × bagging, 100 plants ×2 capitula; mature achene number and % per capitulum, not one flower binary per independently assigned unit. Original study reports open fruit-count lighting z=-2.5 p=.014, bagged p=.140; site/plant clustered SE for common A response not yet recovered.
entries.note: Source model reports statistically resolved ALAN x bagging interaction for percentage of developed fruits (logit beta=-1.40, SE=.592, p=.018) and count p=.014, but this compares exclusion of ALL animal visitors, not nocturnal-only dependence. Count interaction sign in mirrored text conflicts with figure and remains unverified; never pool as logRR.

entries.short_title: Wilson yucca direct lights and skyglow recruitment
entries.screening_reason: 2019 California 5 original sites x 3 transects each, randomly assigned 8 directly lit and 7 control transects. 60 chosen yucca plants, 2 without blooms excluded, fruit set analysis n=58 plants. Adult-moth light trap is a separate 6th site/crossover experiment. Ambient skyglow is an observational gradient. Original fruit model has positive illuminance coefficient but 85-percent CI only, treatment coefficient not robust; effect scale, fruit denominator and transect-level covariance unverified.
entries.note: This is ONE published study with a directly manipulated fecundity component; published Wilson 2020 thesis chapter 2 is source overlap not second experiment. Original species Hesperoyucca whipplei pollinated by diurnal Tegeticula maculata maculata, not observed nocturnal moth dependence; do NOT code V=0 without day/night exclusion.
